# Create a health dataset

```{r}
health <- data.frame(
  Sector = paste0("Sector_", 1:20),

  Population = c(
    12000, 15000, 18000, 20000, 22000,
    25000, 27000, 30000, 32000, 35000,
    38000, 40000, 42000, 45000, 48000,
    50000, 52000, 55000, 58000, 60000
  ),

  Health_Facilities = c(
    1, 2, 2, 3, 2, 3, 2, 4, 3, 4,
    3, 4, 5, 4, 5, 4, 5, 6, 5, 6
  ),

  Poverty_Rate = c(
    45, 40, 38, 35, 42, 33, 39, 30, 34, 28,
    32, 25, 27, 24, 29, 22, 25, 20, 23, 18
  ),

  Distance = c(
    8, 6, 7, 5, 9, 4, 8, 3, 6, 4,
    5, 3, 4, 2, 5, 3, 2, 2, 3, 1
  ),

  Community_Deaths = c(
    35, 38, 44, 42, 50, 48, 55, 52, 59, 57,
    64, 60, 67, 65, 72, 69, 75, 73, 79, 77
  )
)

# Display the dataset
print(health)
```
# check relationship between Depandent variable and independent variables

library(ggplot2)
```{r}
ggplot(data = health, aes(y = Community_Deaths, x = Population)) + geom_point(color = "blue") + 
labs(
  title = "Relationship between Community_Deaths and population",
  y = "Community_Deaths",
  x = "population"
)+ 
 theme_classic()
```
# Check dataset structure
```{r}
str(health)
```

# Summary statistics
```{r}
summary(health)
```
#Fit a multiple linear regression model
```{r}
model <- lm(
  Community_Deaths ~ Population +
    Health_Facilities +
    Poverty_Rate +
    Distance,
  data = health
)
summary (model)
```
# Interpretation : Population has a positive and statistically significant association with community deaths.Holding the other variables constant, an increase of 1,000 people in population is associated with an estimated increase of 1.09.
# Population has a positive and statistically significant association with community deaths.
# other variables (health facilities, poverty_rate and distance)and intercept are statistical insignificant at the 5 %.



# Display regression coefficients
```{r}
coef(model)
```

# Confidence intervals
```{r}
confint(model)
```

# Predicted values
```{r}
fitted(model)
```

# Residuals
```{r}
residuals(model)
```

# Model R-squared
```{r}
summary(model)$r.squared
```

# Adjusted R-squared
```{r}
summary(model)$adj.r.squared
```

#Check assumption
```{r}
plot(model)
```

Summary: Characteristics of a good regression model
Characteristic	What we expect
R-squared	Relatively high
Adjusted R-squared	Relatively high
F-statistic	Statistically significant
P-values	Relevant predictors statistically significant
Multicollinearity	No serious multicollinearity
Homoscedasticity	Constant residual variance
Normality	Approximately normal residuals for classical inference
Autocorrelation	No problematic autocorrelation
RMSE	Relatively low
Prediction performance	Good performance on unseen data
